critical_code_review_comments: shops.py: hire_employee correctly validates role against EMPLOYEE_ROLES, enforces MAX_EMPLOYEES_PER_SHOP cap, does case-insensitive regex.escape(uname) lookup, guards status=='active', blocks self-hire and duplicate active player. Good defensive coverage.

shops.py: employees list/hire/fire/ledger use _owned_shop_or_error which returns 404 for unknown shop and 403 for non-owner — no admin bypass, which is correct for a per-owner UI. Verified admin cannot see rep_tester's shop employees or ledger.

ShopPayoutsPanel/Section math: totals['wages'] and totals['restock'] are set to NEGATIVE values in the backend (totals['wages'] = -int(sum)), then totals['net'] subtracts them again (net = npc + player - wages - restock). With wages=-300 and net = 800+16400-(-300)-... — this would double-count. HOWEVER live results confirm net=16,800 which is 800+16400-300-100 so the frontend is receiving positive wages/restock. Re-reading: `totals['wages'] = -int(row.get('gold', 0))` where gold on shop_wage transactions is stored as a NEGATIVE (debit) — so -int(negative) yields a positive. This works but is fragile: if a future migration ever stores shop_wage as a positive number, totals['wages'] will flip sign and net will overshoot. Recommend adding a comment or asserting sign of the source rows, or use abs(). Not a blocker — behavior is currently correct.
ShopStaffPanel.js keys the NPC-vs-PLAYER badge off `emp.player_user_id` (falsy => NPC). Correct per task note about legacy rows lacking `kind`. Mobile ShopStaffSection.tsx does the same. Good parity.

Wage constant is 50g on both surfaces (WAGE = 50 in JS component, WAGE = 50 in TS component, EMPLOYEE_WAGE from npc_economy on backend). Kept in sync manually — consider surfacing via /api/config or a single source-of-truth constant to guard against future drift.
